concept.name: Transaction finality
concept.definition: Transaction finality is the point at which a transaction's inclusion in the chain becomes irreversible — on proof-of-stake Ethereum, when the block containing it sits under checkpoints justified and finalized by ≥2/3 of staked ETH, so reversal would require burning at least one-third of all stake.
concept.intuition: Finality is when 'pending' becomes 'set in stone' — before it, the chain can still be rewritten; after it, reversal would cost attackers billions.
concept.mechanics: Ethereum divides time into 32-slot epochs; validators vote on checkpoint pairs, and a checkpoint with a two-thirds supermajority becomes justified, then finalized when the next checkpoint is justified (~2 epochs, ≈13 minutes). In proof-of-work chains finality is only probabilistic: confidence grows with each confirmation but never becomes absolute.
concept.failure_modes: If >1/3 of stake goes offline or votes against finality, the chain stalls and the inactivity leak must burn dissenting stake to recover; bridges and exchanges that credit deposits before finality are exposed to reorg double-spends.
concept.misconceptions: One confirmation is not finality — recent blocks can be reorganized. PoS finality is economic, not absolute: reversal is possible in principle if attackers are willing to be mass-slashed.
concept.example: An exchange crediting ETH deposits waits for finalization (~15 minutes): reverting a finalized deposit would require an attacker to get at least one-third of all staked ETH destroyed, an economically irrational cost.
